rows.answer:
Finding reputable, unbiased news sources is definitely an important part of staying informed about global events. I've done some digging based on industry benchmarks and can share a few reliable options with you:

1. Reuters: Known as one of the most trusted news organizations globally, Reuters provides objective news and in-depth analysis from multiple perspectives.

URL: https://www.reuters.com/

2. Associated Press (AP): As the world's oldest newsgatherer, AP is known for its high-quality journalism across various platforms, with a focus on national politics and federal agencies.

URL: https://apnews.com/

3. BBC News: A UK-based public service broadcaster offering reliable global news and analysis, including politics, business, technology, and more.

URL: https://www.bbc.com/news

4. The Wall Street Journal (WSJ): Focused on U.S. politics, markets, and economics, WSJ provides in-depth insights from reputable journalists.

URL: https://www.wsj.com/

5. The New York Times (NYT): Known for its extensive coverage of national and international news, NYT offers a diverse range of perspectives and voices.

URL: https://www.nytimes.com/

6. ProPublica: As the first non-profit investigative journalism outlet in the U.S., ProPublica focuses on accountability journalism to expose abuses of power.

URL: https://www.propublica.org/

While these sources are considered reputable, it's essential to verify information through multiple credible sources and avoid relying solely on social media platforms for your news consumption. Let me know if you have any questions or if there's anything else I can help you with!

Frontend Architecture:

- Progressive Web App for offline-capability (Why it exists: Users may require uninterrupted access to their data during unconnected periods, Why your recommendation wins: Service Workers allow PWA capabilities without JavaScript, Why alternatives exist: None for maintaining offline functionality)

API Architecture:
- RESTful API with JSON responses (Why it exists: Compatibility with existing clients and familiarity to developers, Why your recommendation wins: Widely used and has good support from libraries like Axios, Why alternatives exist: GraphQL)
- Authentication and authorization via JWT tokens stored in browser cookies (Why it exists: Simplifies user experience by avoiding additional round-trips, Why your recommendation wins: JWT is widely supported and requires minimal changes to existing code, Why alternatives exist: OAuth 2.0)

Multi-tenant Architecture:
- Shared database schema with unique instance tables for each tenant (Why it exists: Supports efficient querying across all tenants, Why your recommendation wins: Avoids performance degradation caused by excessive joins and simplifies scaling, Why alternatives exist: Containerization of databases per tenant)
